findings.title: In-place downsize can corrupt the upload and the result is ignored
findings.body: The new loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize with the same path for input and output (tempfile.path to tempfile.path) and ignores the boolean it returns. ImageMagick convert cannot safely read and write one file: it often truncates the destination before the source is fully read, so a failed or partial convert destroys the upload. The open Tempfile still refers to the original inode, so after convert replaces the path, tempfile.size and whatever Upload.create_for reads from the handle can stay on the old bytes or sit past the new EOF. The loop then either keeps shrinking a stale size or stores a corrupt/empty/original image. If convert or ImageOptim fails, execution still falls through to Upload.create_for. Five 80% passes also only reach about a third of the linear dimensions, so a file can remain over SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb and still be uploaded.

findings.title: Oversized GIFs lose animation and SVGs are sent through convert
findings.body: Auto-downsize always goes through OptimizedImage.downsize, whose non-animated instructions run convert with [0] (first frame only). The animated/gifsicle path is selected only when the filesystem path matches /\.GIF$/i. Rack and FileHelper temp paths do not keep the original filename extension, and this call never copies the bytes to a path ending in .gif, so allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails never takes effect. Every oversized GIF is flattened to one frame and that result is what gets stored as the original upload, even when animated thumbnails are allowed. The same branch also runs for any FileHelper.is_image? filename, including SVG, unlike OptimizedImage.create_for which copies SVGs instead of converting them. convert will fail or rasterize the SVG and that output is then saved under the original .svg name.

findings.title: Second downsize definition replaces the width/height method
findings.body: Ruby does not overload methods. The new downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts) at this line replaces the downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) defined just above, so that width/height version never runs. Existing callers that pass numeric max width and height (the previous public signature, which this file still tries to keep) will bind the width to dimensions and the height to opts. optimize then evaluates opts[:allow_animation] and raises NoMethodError, or, if a hash is passed in the height slot, builds a geometry of just the width (for example "1024") instead of "1024x768". Thumbnail generation that still uses the old arity breaks. self.optimize's signature changed the same way (dimensions string instead of width, height), so any external optimize caller is broken too.

findings.title: Client upload limit is hardcoded and ignores per-type site settings
findings.body: validateUploadedFile used to enforce Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so images and attachments had independent admin limits. It now always rejects above 10 * 1024 KB and no longer uses type. Attachments larger than max_attachment_size_kb but under 10MB are sent and then fail (or are stored, if the server trusts the client). Images the admin allowed above 10MB are blocked in the composer even though they would not need downsizing. The 413 handler at line 246 has the same hardcode, so a proxy rejection is reported as a 10MB limit even when nginx or max_image_size_kb is different. uploads_controller.rb also downloads API URLs with a fixed 10.megabytes cap, so raising max_image_size_kb above 10MB cannot be honored on that path either.
